title: 빵집에서: 포장하세요? 봉투 필요하세요?
objective: Order bread, say how many you want, and understand and answer staff questions that use -(으)세요, such as 포장하세요? and 봉투 필요하세요?
summary: Buy bread at a Korean bakery and understand the polite questions staff ask you.
setting: A neighborhood bakery in Korea, in the morning. A customer comes to the counter to buy salt butter rolls and a loaf of sliced bread to take home.

task.title: Order and answer politely
task.line: Staff use -(으)세요 to ask you politely: if the verb stem ends in a vowel, add 세요; if it ends in a consonant, add 으세요.

words.exampleMeaning: Salt butter rolls are really tasty.

words.meaning: loaf of bread (for toast or sandwiches)
to pack food to take away
words.exampleMeaning: Please pack the leftover food for me to take away.
I put the milk in the bag.

words.meaning: no, thanks (politely saying no to an offer)
words.exampleMeaning: Do you want more water? — No, thanks.

dialogue.meaning: Hello. Do you have salt butter rolls?
Yes, they just came out of the oven. They're nice and warm.

dialogue.korean: 그럼 소금빵 세 개 주세요. 이 식빵도 하나 주세요.
dialogue.meaning: Then three salt butter rolls, please. And one of these loaves of bread too.
No, thanks. I have a bag.

exercises: Choose the form a staff member uses with a customer: 손님, 영수증 (필요해요 / 필요하세요)?
Fill in the blank with the polite form of 찾다 (to look for): 손님, 무슨 빵 ____?
Who says it, the staff member or the customer? ① 단팥빵 하나 주세요. ② 카드로 계산하세요? ③ 이거 반으로 잘라 주세요.
Choose the right word for the blank (방금 / 봉투 / 포장): 이 빵은 ____ 나왔어요. 아직 따뜻해요.
answers: ① Customer ② Staff ③ Customer
